content.title: About
content.content: Pot pie, no meat is a baked pie with a flaky crust and a filling of vegetables, legumes and aromatic spices. It is suitable for vegetarians and anyone looking for a lighter alternative to traditional meat pies.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Classic American pot pie is usually made with chicken, but the vegetarian version keeps the creamy sauce.
Mushrooms are often used to mimic a "meaty" texture.
Legumes such as peas or chickpeas add protein and make the dish more filling.
The crust can be made with whole‑grain flour, increasing fiber content.
Meat‑free pot pies are popular in colder months as a comforting warm meal.

items.title: Rich in vegetables
items.content: The vegetable mix (carrot, celery, onion) provides vitamins A, C and K as well as antioxidants.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Legumes contribute complete plant protein, beneficial for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Fiber from vegetables and whole‑grain crust supports digestion and satiety.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Absence of meat reduces saturated fat, which is favorable for heart health.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Mushrooms and legumes are good sources of non‑heme iron, important for blood formation.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to peas, chickpeas or other legumes used in the filling.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces can be salty; people monitoring sodium should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Gluten in crust
items.content: Traditional crust contains wheat; a gluten‑free alternative is needed for celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The pie can be calorie‑dense due to butter‑based sauce and crust; portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat the pie in the oven or microwave until the crust is golden. Serve hot, optionally garnished with fresh herbs or a light yogurt sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked pie in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags for up to 2 months. Ensure it is thoroughly heated before consumption.
